title: How a Helicopter Works in 60 Seconds 🚁🌀 #shorts
description:
Every helicopter rotor blade is a wing, spinning hundreds of times a minute. The pilot climbs by twisting all blades at once, steers by tilting the whole rotor disc, and the tail rotor stops the body from spinning the other way. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#helicopter #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A helicopter has *spinning wings*. Its rotor blades whirl around hundreds of times every minute.

steps.label: Lift
steps.text: Each blade is shaped like a wing. As it slices through the air, it pushes air *down*, and the helicopter goes up.

steps.label: Collective
steps.text: To climb, the pilot raises the *collective*. Every blade twists to a steeper angle at once, making more lift.

steps.label: Swashplate
steps.text: Below the rotor sits the *swashplate*. Rods from this tilting plate change each blade's angle as it spins.

steps.label: Cyclic
steps.text: Push the *cyclic* stick and the whole rotor disc tilts. Lift now leans forward, and so does the helicopter.

steps.label: Tail rotor
steps.text: Spinning the rotor tries to twist the body the *opposite way*. The tail rotor pushes sideways to stop it.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Spin, tilt, *balance*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
